title: A model-screened copper pattern was lowest in a MoS₂ structure search
summary: In a search of 14,715 intercalated structures, a fine-tuned model identified a dice-like arrangement of copper between molybdenum disulfide layers at about 11 atomic% copper. Density-functional calculations confirmed that this candidate was the lowest-energy arrangement among the checked structures, with a binding energy of −0.21 eV per copper atom.
ai_technology: MatterSim v1.0.0-5M fine-tuned atomistic force field; DFT checks

evidence.tested: The learned force field screened and relaxed enumerated structures. Density-functional calculations reevaluated selected low-energy configurations that were outside the model’s training data.
evidence.unknown: The finding is computational and constrained to the searched cells and compositions. The predicted arrangement was not directly observed in a functioning device. The paper defines this copper concentration as Cu atoms divided by all atoms; its MoS₂Cu₀.₁₁ shorthand is not a conventional Cu-per-Mo stoichiometric coefficient.
evidence.ai_role: A fine-tuned MatterSim force field made it feasible to relax and rank the enumerated configurations before DFT was applied to the leading candidates.
